title: FNM-Trans: Efficient FPGA-based Transformer Architecture with Full N: M Sparsity
problem: Transformer models have significant computing and memory costs that hinder efficient deployment. Previous studies fail to exploit a unified sparse pattern to accelerate all three Transformer modules (QKV generation, attention computation, and FFN).
motivation: Efficient deployment of Transformer-based applications is critical for practical AI systems across various domains.
method: FNM-Trans is an algorithm-hardware co-design that optimizes all three Transformer modules using N:M sparsity. At the algorithm level, the approach explores the interplay between dynamic and static pruning under high N:M sparsity constraints. At the hardware level, a custom FPGA architecture is developed with a specialized computing engine and softmax module tailored to support varying levels of N:M sparsity patterns.
key_novelty: Unified N:M sparsity pattern that efficiently accelerates all three core Transformer modules (QKV, attention, FFN) with co-designed hardware support.
contributions: Algorithm-hardware co-design framework for Transformer optimization under N:M sparsity constraints
Custom FPGA hardware architecture with specialized computing engine and softmax module for sparse operations
Comprehensive exploration of dynamic and static pruning interplay under high N:M sparsity
Significant performance improvements: 27.13× speedup over Intel i9-9900X and 1.88×-36.51× over existing FPGA Transformers

metrics.speedup: 27.13× vs Intel i9-9900X, 21.24× vs NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti, 1.88×-36.51× vs FPGA-based Transformers
metrics.accuracy: 11.03% improvement under 2:16 attention sparsity and 4:16 weight sparsity

primary_theme: FPGA-based sparse Transformer acceleration with N:M sparsity
